question.problem: Express $\dfrac{\sqrt{y}+2}{\sqrt{z+1}}$ without radicals in the denominator.
question.worked_solution:
We need to remove the radical $\sqrt{z+1}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{z+1}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{y}+2}{\sqrt{z+1}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{y}+2}{\sqrt{z+1}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{z+1}}{\sqrt{z+1}} & = \\ \frac{(\sqrt{y}+2)\sqrt{z+1}}{(\sqrt{z+1})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{y}\cdot \sqrt{z+1}+2\cdot \sqrt{z+1}}{z+1} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{y\cdot (z+1)}+2\sqrt{z+1}}{z+1} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{yz+y}+2\sqrt{z+1}}{z+1}\end{aligned}
$$
